answer_1.quote: Our evaluation spans a variety of tasks. Coding is an important application of LLMs, facilitating the integration with external tools. We use HumanEval  and MBPP , reporting pass@1 accuracy. Math Problem Solving is critical for LLMs, enabling them to aid users in numerical reasoning tasks. We employ GSM8K  for this purpose and report accuracy. Summarization assists users in capturing the essence of a text. We use CNN/DailyMail (CNN/DM)  and XSUM , measuring performance with RougeL . Translation is a crucial NLP task to overcome linguistic barriers, thereby facilitating global communication. We benchmark it using four directions of WMT22  and assess the translation quality via BLEU . Commonsense Reasoning is a key perspective of LLMs for addressing real-world problems. We assess this using CommonsenseQA (CQA)  and StrategyQA (SQA) , reporting accuracy. Factual Knowledge is crucial for fulfilling users' informational needs. We measure this using FActScore , reporting on the proportion of correctly generated atomic facts. Instruction Following reflects the proficiency in responding to diverse user instructions. We use AlpaceEval  to compare model performances, using pairwise Win Rate against the reference model, Text-Davinci-003. Open-ended Text Generation measures the model's capability to produce fluent and coherent content. We utilize datasets including Book , Wikinews , and Wikitext , and evaluate using MAUVE .
answer_1.outputs: The paper evaluates generated outputs across diverse NLG tasks such as code generation, math reasoning, summarization, translation, factual knowledge generation, instruction following, and open-ended text generation.
